author: Nicole Foeller
title: Utility flags warn lawn care enthusiasts of potential hazards - NewsBreak
text:
By Nicole Foeller No media credit provided. ,
6 hours ago
(KODE/KSNF) — Residents planning to fire up the lawn mower may want to watch for potential hazards.
One being utility flags. They’re normally placed in the ground at the request of a homeowner for a project or because a contractor is performing work in the area.
Experts say as people begin seasonal work like mowing, it’s important to keep a safe distance from those markers. If a flag is accidentally knocked down, it’s recommended placing it at the corner of the driveway, so crews can easily see it and refresh the locate ticket.
“Some people will damage a flag or remove them to mow and then they will try to put them back where they think they were and if that contractor shows up on site and sees that the flags are there, they will think it is okay to dig,” said Spire Energy Construction Supervisor Ryan Conley.
One other thing. Having utility flags in your yard does not give you permission to start digging. Homeowners still need to request their own locate ticket.
